newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: EU signs cooperation pacts with Laos, Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: EU signs cooperation pacts with Laos, Cambodia.

text.p: The European Union on Tuesday signed cooperation deals strengthening links in a range of areas with Cambodia and Laos.
The deals represent the first contractual relations between the Union and the two countries. Diplomatic ties with Laos were established in 1986 and with Cambodia in 1992.

The two accords were signed side by side during a meeting of EU foreign ministers to underline the EU's growing interest in the South East Asian region, Dutch Foreign Minister Hans Van Mierlo told the signing ceremony.
"This serves also to highlight further the extent of progress in establishing relations with South East Asian countries," Van Mierlo said.

The pacts, which in common with a generation of cooperation deals signed by the EU and Asian and Latin American countries contains a human rights clause, covers areas from trade, development and the economy to the environment.
